study_identification.title: Neurodevelopmental model of schizophrenia revisited: similarity in individual deviation and idiosyncrasy from the normative model of whole-brain white matter tracts and shared brain-cognition covariation with ADHD and ASD

study_characteristics.study_objective: Construct sex-specific normative models of whole-brain white-matter tract microstructure (GFA) from typically developing controls and quantify individual deviations in schizophrenia, ADHD, and ASD; test similarity/differences across disorders and link deviations to cognition via CCA and exploratory unsupervised analyses.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: One-sample t-tests (with FDR) on tract Z-scores quantified deviation per subgroup; F-tests (variance ratios) quantified idiosyncrasy. Propensity score age matching used for between-group comparisons. Unsupervised machine learning evaluated separability of SCZ vs neurodevelopmental disorders based on WM deviation patterns. Canonical correlation analysis (CCA) linked tract deviation profiles to cognitive measures (Wechsler and CANTAB).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: WM deviation/idiosyncrasy patterns in schizophrenia resemble those in ADHD and ASD, especially at early stages; unsupervised learning could not separate SCZ from neurodevelopmental disorders using WM deviations; CCA revealed shared cognition–WM deviation coupling across diagnoses.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Across 45 tracts, schizophrenia showed more negative GFA deviations and greater idiosyncrasy than ASD/ADHD, with effects increasing from first-episode to chronic stages. Notable tracts with strong effects included fornix (Cohen’s d ≈ −1.04 to −0.44), IFOF (≈ −0.82 to −0.33), frontostriatal pathways (≈ −0.92 to −0.31), thalamic radiations (≈ −0.64 to −0.33), and corpus callosum temporal fibers (≈ −0.70 to −0.28). Idiosyncrasy was prominent in thalamic radiations (F ≈ 1.48–2.87), frontostriatal (≈ 1.40–2.67), and cingulum-hippocampal (≈ 1.61–2.66). Dimensional correlations of deviation/idiosyncrasy patterns were significant between early-stage SCZ and ASD/ADHD (e.g., ρ≈0.41–0.54). Unsupervised clustering based on WM deviations failed to clearly separate SCZ from neurodevelopmental disorders. CCA identified a cross-diagnostic dimension linking deviations in long-range association/sensory relay tracts (e.g., IFOF, ILF, thalamic radiations) to working memory and intellectual functioning.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Single-site, cross-sectional design limits generalizability and causal inference; absence of external validation; smaller subgroup samples reduce power; age and stage effects warrant longitudinal confirmation; some preprocessing details deferred to prior work.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: Sex-stratified normative modeling with nonparametric age smoothing; tract-level z-score deviation and variance-based idiosyncrasy; age propensity score matching for fair comparisons; integration with unsupervised learning and CCA for clinical interpretation.

general_notes.general_notes: Imaging on a single 3T Siemens TIM Trio with DSI (102 directions, bmax 4000); 45 tract atlas on open DSI template; GFA via MAP model; diffeomorphic registration for tract sampling; QC excluded low SNR/high SDC scans; z-scores uncorrelated with age/SNR/motion. SCZ subgroups: FES n=75, subchronic n=161, chronic n=45.
